name: King of Debir
overview: The King of Debir was a male ruler identified as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua, as recorded in Joshua 12:7 and 12:13. No tribal affiliation or additional personal details are provided in Scripture. His role is primarily noted in the context of Israel's conquest under Joshua's leadership.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Debir' literally means 'king of Debir,' indicating his rulership over the city of Debir. This designation is a straightforward title rather than a personal name, and it is not indicated to be a name given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Debir beyond his identification as one of the kings defeated by Joshua.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Debir represents one of the local Canaanite rulers who opposed Israel's divinely sanctioned conquest of the Promised Land. His defeat by Joshua demonstrates God's faithfulness in granting Israel victory over established kingdoms, fulfilling His promises to His people. This figure exemplifies the opposition overcome during Israel's entrance into Canaan, highlighting God's sovereign power in history.
